text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 12.4 driver + kernel roll last night, a subset of west clusters are reporting missing MIG profiles and GPU UUIDs remapped. Batch jobs are failing with container logs saying MIG not found. :frowning:

aj: which nodes specifically? can you paste the output of nvidia-smi -L and nvidia-smi mig -lgip from one of the bad hosts?

maria: pasting from gpu-w1-054 (host ns):
```
nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-abc123)
GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-def456)

nvidia-smi mig -lgip
No MIG devices found
```
but the orchestration shows MIG configs bound to UUIDs that no longer exist and some workloads are landing on GPU:def456 which used to be def456 -> now shows def789 in /sys.

kai: this rings a bell from the 530->535 window. NVML ABI or userland/driver mismatches can make UUIDs appear to shift. are kernel module and userland libs consistent on the host? run dkms status and ldd on nvidia-smi.

maria: quick check: host driver package = 535.86, kernel module 535.86. containers still have old libnvidia-ml from cached base image. suspect container userland vs host mismatch.

aj: if the container exposes an older libnvidia-ml, NVML calls can return inconsistent device lists. quick mitigation: restart nvidia-persistenced and container runtime on the host to force correct bindings, but DO NOT reapply MIG profiles fleet-wide until we confirm lib mismatch. use the helper: /opt/redwood/bin/mig-reapply.sh on a single canary node.

ops-oncall: started canary rollback to driver 530 on gpu-w1-{054,057,061}. moved queued jobs off those hosts. watching queue.

infra-bot: redeploy job started for node gpu-w1-054 (job_id=rd-deploy-8791) — rolling update in progress.

kai: also check ldconfig paths. compare host and container: run ldd /usr/bin/nvidia-smi in host namespace and inside failing container. if they point to different libnvidia-ml.so.* versions, that's the smoking gun.

maria: quick diff I ran on gpu-w1-054:
```
Host: libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 (version 535.86)
Container: libnvidia-ml.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 (version 530.41)
```
matches the hypothesis. container image has older lib shipped from base image.

aj: remediation plan: 1) pin the fleet driver to 530 for now to stop churn, 2) rebuild runtime images to have matching libnvidia binaries (target 535.86) and push canary images, 3) add a post-upgrade healthcheck that runs nvidia-smi mig -lgip and fails the upgrade if MIG discovery differs, 4) add orchestration step to detect UUID remap and trigger a safe migration path that rebinds MIG configs rather than blindly reapplying (to avoid orphaned configs).

maria: opened INFRA-4721 and attached node list, logs, and canary plan. I'll run an audit script that lists all nodes where host driver version != container lib version and output will go to the ticket. @ops-oncall keep the rollback until aj confirms image rebuild is completed.

ops-oncall: watching. how bad is the cost hit?

maria: rough calc: jobs retried over ~8 hours across the pool -> ~120 GPU-hours lost before we caught it. marking incident severity medium.

aj: I'll queue the image rebuild now and update terraform module to gate driver rollouts behind the MIG discovery check. ETA for image rebuild: ~2 hours. after that we'll run staged upgrade: canary hosts -> a small subset -> full fleet.

maria: note for postmortem: capture the chain (driver roll, cached container libs, missing image bump, lack of MIG discovery healthcheck). propose adding a preflight check to the upgrade pipeline that verifies container runtime libs match host driver via ldd comparison.

infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-4721 created and assigned to aj, maria. Severity: medium.

aj: thanks — I'll post status updates in this thread and attach the audit dump when done.

maria: thanks everyone, will follow up after the canary verification. :thumbsup:
